prompt:
I need the front end for Benchbook. A reference-authoring tool a community college's welding technology program uses to write and maintain the shop procedure handbook students consult at their booths.

Who's using it: Rhonda Ekwueme, 51, lead welding instructor at Cascade Valley Community College. She is a certified welding inspector with 25 years in fabrication shops, comfortable with documentation but not a professional writer. She maintains the handbook for about 60 students across first- and second-year cohorts.

What they're doing right now: The program just replaced six of its old MIG machines with new pulse-capable units, and the settings in the 'GMAW – 1/4" mild steel, vertical up (3G)' procedure page are now wrong for half the booths. She is rewriting that page before Monday's lab. That means splitting the parameter section into old-machine and new-machine variants and replacing the outdated photo of the torch angle. She also needs to move the spatter-cleanup step to sit before the bend-test prep, and add a safety callout about pulse-mode arc brightness. She has also found that the page on joint fit-up links to a section that was deleted last term, and she wants to fix that link while she's at it.

What's in the system at this point: The handbook has 23 procedure pages grouped into GMAW, FCAW, SMAW, GTAW and Shop Safety. The 3G GMAW page currently has 9 ordered steps, 2 figures (a torch-angle photo and a weave-pattern diagram), 1 parameter set (wire feed 280 ipm, 19.5 V, 0.035" ER70S-6 wire, 75/25 Ar/CO2 at 30 cfh, 3/8"–1/2" stick-out), 3 safety callouts, and cross-references to 4 other pages. The new machines are 6 Lincoln-style pulse units in booths 7–12, and booths 1–6 keep the old units. Each page carries an author, a last-reviewed date, the course codes that use it (WLD 121, WLD 222), and a status of draft, in review or published. A pending reviewer comment from the department chair on this page reads 'confirm interpass temp note matches AWS D1.1.'

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
